note: Administration Language Negotiation registers a core interface-language negotiation method id 'administration-language-negotiation' (label 'Administration language'), enabled/ordered under language.types negotiation.language_interface.enabled. For users with the permission 'use administration language negotiation' it returns the user's preferred_admin_langcode on matching admin locations. Its settings live in config administration_language_negotiation.negotiation: paths (glob list), admin_routes (bool), use_default_lang (bool). It defines a plugin type administration_language_negotiation_condition (plugins: paths, admin_routes) and a configure route. Cases are grounded in that real config: introspection reads back a custom path / the admin_routes flag; execution enables the negotiation method (writes language.types) and turns on admin_routes, both verified against live config.

evals.prompt: What does the administration_language_negotiation module do, and where do I enable its language detection method on a Drupal 11 site?
evals.expected_output: It adds an interface-language negotiation method 'Administration language' that forces admin pages into each user's preferred admin language. Enable and order it (before other methods) at Configuration > Regional and language > Languages > Detection and selection for the Interface text language.

evals.prompt: Which config object and keys control which pages administration_language_negotiation treats as 'admin', and what are they?
evals.expected_output: Config object administration_language_negotiation.negotiation with keys: paths (a list of glob patterns, default /admin, /admin/*, /node/add/*, ...), admin_routes (bool - treat every admin route as admin), and use_default_lang (bool fallback to site default language).

evals.prompt: Which permission does administration_language_negotiation define, and what does it control?
evals.expected_output: The permission 'use administration language negotiation'. Only users with it get the admin-language negotiation applied and see the core 'Administration pages language' (preferred_admin_langcode) field on their user edit form; it lets non-administrators choose an admin language.

evals.prompt: On this site, an extra admin-language path has been configured in administration_language_negotiation. Inspect the live configuration and give the custom path pattern that has been added to its paths list (beyond the default /admin and /node paths).
evals.expected_output: The custom path is /aln-probe/* (present in administration_language_negotiation.negotiation:paths alongside the defaults).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the administration_language_negotiation settings and state whether the 'admin_routes' option (apply the admin language on every admin route) is currently enabled.
evals.expected_output: Yes - admin_routes is true in administration_language_negotiation.negotiation, so the admin language is applied on every admin route.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, enable the administration_language_negotiation 'Administration language' negotiation method for the interface (interface text) language type, so it participates in interface language detection. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In language.types, negotiation.language_interface.enabled now contains the key 'administration-language-negotiation' (with a weight). Set it e.g. via the Detection and selection UI or by adding the key to the enabled interface methods.

evals.prompt: Configure administration_language_negotiation on this site so that the admin language is applied on every admin route (turn on its 'admin_routes' option). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: administration_language_negotiation.negotiation:admin_routes is set to true (e.g. drush cset administration_language_negotiation.negotiation admin_routes true, or tick it on the module's settings form).
